 Order

The petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504,
506, 307, 114 read with Section 149 of IPC alleging that, the defacto complainant is the legally wedded wife of the accused No.1.
The accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in-law.
The accused Nos.4 to 8 are the relatives of the husband of the accused No.1.
The accused subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also assaulted her.
The cognizance of the aforesaid offences taken by the learned Magistrate is impugned in this petition.
2. Though the respondent No.2 has been served with notice, she has not chosen to appear in person or through her counsel.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State.
4.
The petitioners have produced the certificate of marriage, which indicates that, the defacto complainant has contracted the second marriage on 30.3.2019.
The said marriage is not disputed and is uncontroverted by the respondent No.2.

The petitioners, though have brought to the notice of the Investigating Officer, he has not furnished the same with the Trial Court, and they are unnecessary made to appear before the Trial Court for the last seven years.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1227 5.

Perusal of the FIR lodged by the respondent No.2 indicates that, except the omnibus and general allegations, there is no specific allegation as against each of the petitioners as to how and in what manner they subjected her to cruelty both mentally and physically.
6. In view of the above, I am of the view that the FIR was lodged with an ulterior motive to falsely implicate the petitioners herein to wreak vengeance with revengeful intent.
Hence, the continuation of criminal proceeding will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in SC No.97/2016 pending on the file of the learned District and Sessions Judge, Yadgir, is hereby quashed.
